name: authors-distributed-foundations
description: Principles from the foundational distributed systems literature, restated in Agent ARB's own words with a citation. No text reused; the authors have not reviewed or endorsed this pack.

rules.title: The network is not reliable, fast, secure or homogeneous
rules.requirement: The design does not assume the network is always available, has zero latency, infinite bandwidth, is secure, has a fixed topology, or has one administrator. Each remote call path says what happens when the network is partitioned or slow.

source.name: L. Peter Deutsch and colleagues at Sun Microsystems

rules.title: Choose consistency or availability under partition, explicitly
rules.requirement: For each replicated store the design states what it gives up during a partition, consistency or availability, and why that is acceptable for the data in question.

source.name: Eric Brewer
source.locator: CAP Twelve Years Later: How the Rules Have Changed, IEEE Computer, 2012

rules.title: Cross-service writes avoid distributed transactions
rules.requirement: Where a business operation updates more than one service, the design uses local transactions plus asynchronous messaging, idempotent handlers and compensating actions rather than a two-phase commit across services, or justifies the exception.

source.name: Pat Helland
source.locator: Life beyond Distributed Transactions: an Apostate's Opinion, CIDR 2007

rules.title: Eventual consistency is named where it exists, with its user-visible effect
rules.requirement: Any path where a reader can observe stale data is identified, the expected staleness window is stated, and the design says what the user sees and whether read-your-writes is needed.

source.name: Werner Vogels
source.locator: Eventually Consistent, Communications of the ACM, 2009

rules.title: Latency budgets are built from known operation costs
rules.requirement: The latency objective is decomposed across hops and storage operations using realistic per-operation costs, so the design shows the objective is achievable before it is built.

source.name: Jeff Dean
source.locator: Numbers Everyone Should Know, Stanford CS295 lecture, 2010

rules.title: Logs and streams are the integration backbone, with ordering stated
rules.requirement: Where events are used to move data between services, the design states the ordering guarantee, the partitioning key that provides it, the delivery guarantee, and how consumers handle duplicates.

source.name: Martin Kleppmann
source.locator: Designing Data-Intensive Applications, Chapter 11, Stream Processing
